selectedFunctions.label: Blur borrow NFT-backed lending
warnings: Static source/deployment/ABI metadata only, not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; these nonpayable calls require zero native value.

Only one canonical Blur family is admitted, using its own Ethereum Blend lending proxy, not marketplace/exchange orders. Current EIP-1967 implementation observed at block 26260306 is 0xb258ca5559b11cd702f363796522b04d7722ea56. Sourcify root and implementation report match, not exact_match. UUPS owner upgrades remain possible.

Loan amounts and repayments are 18-decimal ETH-denominated Blur Pool ledger balances, not msg.value or arbitrary ERC20 transfers. Existing pool funding/authorization and NFT approval are prerequisites; none is granted here. Fixed pool immutable is 0x0000000000a39bb272e79075ade125fd351887ac. Pool, linked Helpers library and collateral receiver runtime safety are not independently attested.

Full current lien preimages must hash to the stored lien ID. Annual rates are basis points; debt uses continuous compounding via signed-WAD exponent math, with rounding. No caller repayment maximum or transaction deadline is provided by repay. Auction duration is in blocks, not seconds; starting an auction can lead to collateral default/seizure.

LoanOffer signature bytes are finite existing lender quotes, optionally including a registered oracle signature plus block number. Source EIP-712 domain binds chain and Blend proxy, full loan terms and lender nonce; expiration, salt cancellation, per-loan bounds and cumulative capacity are checked. Bytes are parsed only for ecrecover, never executable calldata. No backend quote/permit/wallet signing, oracle registration or operator permission is introduced.

Locks caller NFT into Blend and creates caller-owned borrower lien; transfers signed offer lender Blur Pool balance to caller. Rate <=100000 bps, loan min/max and remaining aggregate offer capacity apply; auction duration <=432000 blocks. No marketplace order or arbitrary callback payload.

# Overview

The Blur foundation aims to facilitate community-led governance and participation in the DAO and assist contributors with the development and growth of the Blur ecosystem, including, but not limited to: the Blur marketplace, aggregators, and lending protocol ([Blend](https://twitter.com/blur_io/status/1653051809240604674?s=20)).

The BLUR token gives the community control over the DAO and allows the community to actively participate in governance. 

* [Governance](/governance.md)
* [Tokenomics](/tokenomics.md)
* [Contracts](/contracts.md)

devdoc.details: This contract implements an upgradeable proxy. It is upgradeable because calls are delegated to an implementation address that can be changed. This address is stored in storage in the location specified by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967[EIP1967], so that it doesn't conflict with the storage layout of the implementation behind the proxy.

constructor.details: Initializes the upgradeable proxy with an initial implementation specified by `_logic`. If `_data` is nonempty, it's used as data in a delegate call to `_logic`. This will typically be an encoded function call, and allows initializating the storage of the proxy like a Solidity constructor.

devdoc.details: This contract implements an upgradeable proxy. It is upgradeable because calls are delegated to an implementation address that can be changed. This address is stored in storage in the location specified by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967[EIP1967], so that it doesn't conflict with the storage layout of the implementation behind the proxy.

constructor.details: Initializes the upgradeable proxy with an initial implementation specified by `_logic`. If `_data` is nonempty, it's used as data in a delegate call to `_logic`. This will typically be an encoded function call, and allows initializating the storage of the proxy like a Solidity constructor.
